symptom: Every catalog refresh rebuilt every table from every unit after any save: about 4.5 s of decoding and inserting on a 4,753-unit app, most of it for rows identical to the cached ones (5.6-8 s end to end per refresh)
cause: The builder had no record of which unit a row came from, so it could neither keep an unchanged unit's rows nor drop a changed unit's; every pass listed and decoded every document of its type
file: `mdl/catalog/builder_tx.go` (`builderTx` / `Stmt` record rowid ranges per owner), `mdl/catalog/builder_incremental.go` (`loadPrevious`, `planIncremental`, `dependentUnits`, `dropRebuiltRows`, `verifyIncremental`, `persistOwners`, `clearCatalog`), `mdl/catalog/builder.go` (`buildOn`, `buildAttempt`, phase list), `own()` at the head of every per-document loop, `mdl/backend/modelsdk/units.go` (`WithUnitScope`), `modelsdk/mpr/reader_units.go` (`ListUnitsByTypeWhere`)
insight: **Record ownership where rows are written, not per table.** A wrapper on the build's transaction notes the rowid range of every INSERT under the pass's current owner, so 130 insert sites needed no change. The per-document loops each call `own(unit)`, and a row written while the pass is skipping a document fails the build back to a full one, which caught a bug on its own: the backend lists System enumerations that are no units. Start from the cached catalog (sqlite3_deserialize) and delete the rebuilt units' rows rather than copying the kept ones: copying re-tokenized every carried full-text row and cost more than the rest of the build. Deserializing the same connection twice crashed SQLite (modernc) once its full-text tables had been used, so plan on a scratch copy of the same bytes and empty the tables with DELETE to fall back. The equivalence test passed its control at first because mxcli edits rewrite the documents that name what they change; only a step where a document's rows change while its unit does not (a delete over a repointed association) shows the dependents are needed
fix: Rebuild only changed units and the documents whose refs name them (members by prefix, specializations transitively), list and decode only those through a unit-scoped backend view, verify after the build that no document names a changed unit's new names (else widen once), fall back to a full build for units no per-unit pass reads (folders, modules, settings, security, navigation). Tests: `TestCatalog_IncrementalBuildEqualsFullBuild` and `TestCatalog_IncrementalFastBuildEqualsFullBuild` (every table vs a forced full build over 19 edit steps, chained incrementally), the source test, and unit tests for ranges, the skipped-document error and dependents
